practiceProblems.title: Creating Arrays
practiceProblems.description:
In Rust, arrays are used to store multiple values in a single variable, instead of declaring separate variables for each value.

To declare an array, 
- Define the variable type, 
- Specify the name of the array followed by square brackets and 
- Specify the number of elements it should store.

E.g
   
     let cars = ["Ferrari", "Volvo", "Lambo", "Tesla"];

### Task
Write a program which does the following
- Create an Array of the first 5 positive integers
- Once the array is define - output "Done" to the console.

constraints:

- $1 \leq N \leq 100$
- $1 \leq M \leq N\cdot(N-1)/2$
- $1 \leq u_i, v_i \leq N$
- $u_i \neq v_i$ for each $1 \leq i \leq M$.
- The sum of $N$ over all test cases won't exceed $100$.
practiceProblems.inputFormat:
- The first line of input will contain a single integer $T$, denoting the number of test cases.
- Each test case consists of multiple lines of input.
    - The first line of each test case contains two space-separated integers $N$ and $M$ — the number of vertices and edges of the graph, respectively.
    - The next $M$ lines describe the edges. The $i$-th of these $M$ lines contains two space-separated integers $u_i$ and $v_i$, denoting an edge between $u_i$ and $v_i$.
practiceProblems.outputFormat: For each test case, output on a new line the number of good subgraphs of $G$, modulo $10^9 + 7$.

practiceProblems.title: Changing the elements of an Array
practiceProblems.description:
To change the value of a specific element, we can refer to the index number.

### Task
Write a program which does the following
- The 3rd month in the given list is incorrect
- Update the 3rd month in the given array with the correct one - "Mar" 
- Once the $3^{rd}$ array element is updated, output the $3^{rd}$ array element to the console

practiceProblems.title: Displaying the count of elements
practiceProblems.description:
To get the length of an array in Rust, you can use the len() method:
For e.g.
  
              let my_numbers = [10, 20, 30, 40, 50];
              println!("{}", my_numbers.len());
              // Result: 5

**Note** 
- The len() method returns the number of elements in the array, not the size of the array in bytes.
- To get the size in bytes, you would multiply the length by the size of the array element type. For example, if the array was of type i32, each element would typically be 4 bytes, so the total size in bytes would be 4 times the number of elements.

### Task
Write a program which does the following
- Create an i32 array containing the elements - 10, 20, 30, 40, 50, 60
- Compile and output to the console the accurate count of the number of integer elements in the given array.
